title: A ring map smooth at a chart prime gives a principal smooth scheme neighbourhood
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ be affine open subschemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $f(W)\subseteq V$, and let $\varphi:R\to A$ be the induced ring map. Let $x\in W$ correspond to a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset A$. Suppose $\varphi$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], meaning that some $g_0\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ makes $R\to A_{g_0}$ a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then there exists $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $R\to A_g$ is smooth and, for the principal open $W_g=D(g)\subset W$ canonically identified with $\operatorname{Spec}A_g$, the restriction $f|_{W_g}:W_g\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. In particular $W_g$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$.

source.place: Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, affine comparison and infinitesimal lifting criterion, applied to a principal affine source neighbourhood and its original open target; the final affine-to-scheme passage in the proof of Morphisms lemma-smooth-at-point.

proof.text: By the definition of smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal], choose the given witness $g=g_0\notin\mathfrak q$ with $R\to A_g$ smooth. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $R\to A$ is needed: smoothness is assumed only after localization.

By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], the localization map induces an open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}A_g\to W$ with image $W_g=D(g)$. Thus it gives the stated canonical identification with $W_g$. Since $g\notin\mathfrak q$, $x\in D(g)$ by the definition of a principal open. This is open in $X$ because $W$ is open in $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], $f|_{W_g}$ factors uniquely as $h:W_g\to V$ followed by $V\hookrightarrow S$. Under the affine identifications, $h$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to A_g)$: [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies $W\to V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$, and functoriality identifies its composite with the localization morphism with the spectrum of $R\to A\to A_g$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] to the smooth map $R\to A_g$. Its spectrum is smooth in the scheme sense of the item. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], applied to the canonical affine identifications in step 2, therefore makes $h:W_g\to V$ smooth.

source.place: Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, affine comparison; Morphisms Tag 01V6

proof.text: Apply clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] with the original $f:X\to S$, $U=W_g$ and the original target open $V$. Its hypotheses hold by step 2, and its restricted map $f_{U,V}=h$ is smooth by step 3. It follows that $f|_{W_g}:W_g\to S$ is smooth. Together with $g\notin\mathfrak q$, smoothness of $R\to A_g$, and the neighbourhood assertion in step 2, this gives every required clause.
